 CORAM: HONOURABLE MR. JUSTICE CHANDRA SHEKHAR JHA
ORAL ORDER 4 11-12-2024 Heard learned counsel appearing on behalf of the parties.

2. The present matter was taken on board for considering the prayer of bail and suspension of sentence of above named appellant/convict during pendency of appeal under Section 389(1) of the Code of Criminal Procedure (in short Cr.P.C.) as raised through present petition, which filed in present appeal, preferred under Section 374(2) of the Cr.P.C. against the judgment of conviction dated 20.05.2024 and order of sentence dated 22.05.2024, rendered by the learned Additional District Judge VI Cum Special Judge (POCSO), Purnea in Special Case No. 100/2022 arising out of K. Nagar P.S. Case No. 370/2022, where learned trial court Patna High Court CR.

APP (SJ) No.3202 of 2024(4) dt.11-12-2024 has charged appellant for offences under Section 376 of the Indian Penal Code and Sections 4 and 6 of the POCSO Act but convicted the appellant for the offence under Section 354 of the Indian Penal Code and Section 8 of the POCSO Act.

Appellant was sentenced to undergo one year of rigorous imprisonment and fine of Rs. 5000/- for the offence under Section 354 of the Indian Penal Code and for the offence under Section 8 of the POCSO Act, ordered to undergo rigorous imprisonment for five years alongwith fine of Rs. 25,000/-(Rupees Twenty Five Thousand)
and in default of payment of fine, he shall further undergo simple imprisonment for three months.
All sentences shall ordered to run concurrently.

3. Learned counsel appearing on behalf of the appellant/convict submitted that the testimony of victim, who testified before the learned trial court as PW-6 categorically suggest that the appellant/convict committed rape upon her on point of knife but same was not believed by the Md. Mojahid Islam vs The State Of Bihar on 11 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/115840749/
1 learned trial court and, thereafter, the appellant/convict was acquitted for the charge of penetrative sexual assault/rape.

sentences.text: It is Patna High Court CR.
APP (SJ) No.3202 of 2024(4) dt.11-12-2024 submitted that the conviction was made under Section 8 of the POCSO Act, where sentence was imposed as five years rigorous imprisonment.
It is submitted that finding of learned trial court with same set of evidence qua sexual assault appears questionable.
It is submitted that though victim as per her school certificate appears minor but as per medical examination, she found between the age group of 18-20 years.

While concluding the argument, it is submitted that the appellant remains in custody for about two years and four months i.e. almost about half of the sentence against five years rigorous imprisonment, wherein this appeal is of July 2024 itself and same is not likely to be heard finally in near future, accordingly appellant/convict deserves bail on this score alone.

In support of aforesaid submission, learned counsel relied upon the full Bench report of this Court in the matter Anurag Baitha Vs. State of Bihar reported in AIR 1987 Pat 274(FB):1987 PLJR 485 (FB) and also Atul @ Ashutosh Vs. State of Madhya Pradesh , (2024) 3 SCC 663.
4.

sentences.text: Learned APP duly assisted by learned counsel Md. Patna High Court CR. APP (SJ) No.3202 of 2024(4) dt.11-12-2024 Hussain appearing on behalf of the informant, while opposing the prayer of bail and suspension of sentence submitted that victim specifically deposed as to commit sexual assault upon her on point of knife, however he could not disputed the factual submission including custody period, as submitted above by learned counsel appearing for the appellant.

5. In view of aforesaid factual and legal submission and by taking note of fact as the appellant remains in custody for about two years and four months i.e. almost about half of the sentence, where this appeal is of July, 2024 itself, which cannot be taken on board for final hearing in near future,
accordingly, above named accused/appellant is directed to be released on bail, during the pendency of the appeal, furnishing bail bond of Rs. 10,000/- (Rupees Ten Thousand) with two sureties of the like amount each to the satisfaction of learned Additional District Judge VI Cum Special Judge (POCSO), Purnea in Special Case No. 100/2022 arising out of K. Nagar P.S. Case No. 370/2022.
6.
The sentence imposed by the concerned trial court shall remain suspended during pendency of appeal.
Patna High Court CR.
APP (SJ) No.3202 of 2024(4) dt.11-12-2024 Realization of fine be also kept in abeyance, till disposal of appeal.
7. The appellant shall co-operate in disposal of the appeal.

8. Observation, as regard to merit, if any, shall be of no bearing while final hearing of this appeal,
being prima facie observation.
9.
Re -notify this case as per its own seriatim for final hearing.

(Chandra Shekhar Jha, J) veena/-
